decision: Do not promote float64-acos cast as universal Torch CPU parity remedy.
scope: Independent Apple Silicon original-operation characterization; no production changes.

input_generation.boundaries: cos(degrees)**2 cast float32 for each integer degree0..90, neighboring +/-64 float32 bit patterns clipped to [0,1]

observations.reported_failing_point_M1: all three expressions return1057360530; existing M1 expression already matches originalCPU at this point

source_evidence.header_observation: acos uses Sleef_acosf4_u10; this is source evidence for a backend-specific approximation, not proof of runtime dispatch.

recommendation: Characterize actual pinned Torch CPU backend on each supported platform; restore upstream float32 sqrt then its acos behavior in one bounded CPU-native helper used by both paths. If precision-only repair passes full boundary classifiers and all unchanged field gates per platform, qualify evidence to those profiles; do not assert global bit parity. Otherwise reproduce the pinned native math algorithm explicitly rather than shift inputs or change comparisons.
